strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime brings existing provider-failure retry admission into the headless continuation boundary without provider execution.
Headless callers can continue from provider failure evidence to an explicitly runnable retry task without caller-side task.start orchestration.

Continuation decisions and retry provenance remain bounded and replayable without raw prompts, provider responses, request bodies, file content, command output, environment values, secrets, or raw paths.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances llm_provider_execution with supporting headless_autonomous_development and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.continue_once accepts a bounded llm_provider_failure_retry_source and creates or replays one retry task through the existing provider retry admission path.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M13.2 direct task.start admission requires external controllers to switch protocols; it does not provide stale-progress validation, continuation replay, or next-route selection inside headless.continue_once.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Provider failures remain a dead end for the headless loop, forcing caller-owned recovery policy after structured provider failure outcomes.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M18.3 handled approved recovery proposal apply, M19.1 handled direct task.run context budgets, and M19.2 carried context budgets into headless execution; M20.1 handles provider retry admission in headless continuation.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.continue_once request/result contract is extended; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new admission field is operational bounded retry-admission evidence, not a report/history/readiness surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: After stale-progress validation, the runtime delegates to existing provider retry admission, creates or replays a retry task, records a headless continuation decision, and returns an explicit retry-task run route.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can advance one provider recovery step using the same replay-safe headless contract used for other recovery boundaries.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the first M20 slice; M20.2 should run the admitted retry task through existing task.run/provider gates.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts llm_provider_failure_retry_source without adding a new RPC
valid provider retry evidence creates exactly one retry task through the existing provider retry admission path
same continuation_id replays the bounded admission without duplicate TaskStarted, TaskRunning, provider request, provider failure, or headless decision events
stale progress rejects before retry task creation or decision mutation
invalid authorization and incompatible multi-step or recovery-field combinations reject before mutation
next_route.kind is run_llm_provider_retry_task_explicitly and M20.1 does not run the retry task or call a provider

ledger and RPC results contain bounded identifiers/provenance only and no raw prompt, provider response, request body, file content, stdout, stderr, command, environment, secret, absolute path, or canonical path
VSIX protocol validators accept valid provider retry admission params/result payloads and reject raw-data-bearing payloads

tests: VSIX headless provider retry admission validator cases

next_phase_candidate_notes: After M20.1 merge, plan M20.2 to run the admitted LLM provider retry task through existing task.run provider, network, sensitive-prompt, and AccessNetwork permission gates. Reject provider retry reports, histories, readiness wrappers, and automatic provider calls.
